I've written the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. The bundle comes to 267 bytes min+gzip, with 101 bytes of your own code. The size command can't run on the original `src/module.ts` because `lodash` isn't installed, so I have no baseline to compare against. I haven't run the original against the new file on any inputs.

- **`publicFields`:** it uses `pick` from `es-toolkit`, called the same way as the lodash `pick`.
- **`totalAge`:** it uses `sumBy` from `es-toolkit`, with `(row) => row.age` in place of lodash's `'age'` shorthand. Both return 0 for an empty array.
- **`parseAmount`:** it uses `toNumber` from `es-toolkit/compat`, because the main `es-toolkit` entry has no `toNumber`. The compat version is just `Number(value)`. Lodash's `toNumber` also special-cases `0b…`, `0o…` and signed hex strings, but your input alphabet has no `b` or `o`. For signed hex like `-0x1`, `Number` also gives `NaN`, the same as lodash.

I removed the `lodash` imports entirely, and kept the exported signatures, `Row`, and `Config` unchanged.

I couldn't confirm that type checking passes. The project's own `tsc` run only reported errors in `src/module.ts` (the missing `lodash` modules), and I don't know whether `tsconfig.json` includes `out/`. A separate strict `tsc` run on `out/module.ts` hit two `es-toolkit` declaration errors (`Disposable`, `AsyncDisposable`) from my compiler flags, so it didn't settle the question either.
